recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-20394; future changes to questionnaire-unitOption or questionnaire-unitValueSet descriptions should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack, with SDC IG work only if off-list-unit behavior is being changed.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Questionnaire issue asking that unitOption and unitValueSet extension descriptions directly state that, when either extension is present, Quantity units are constrained to the listed units and should be treated as a required binding rather than an extensible binding.
initial_application: Core commit f7b451ebc666a31afcf389ade7e375399269b176, merged by 596ab9615af497ab90973db507be9054794bf2fb, updated source/questionnaire/questionnaire-extensions-spreadsheet.xml for both unitOption and unitValueSet with the required/not-extensible wording requested by the Jira resolution.
additional_context: The current core build still includes Questionnaire, but the unit extension StructureDefinitions were intentionally removed from core by dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 and now belong to the FHIR Extension Pack. The Extension Pack IG includes input/definitions/* and its current unitOption and unitValueSet definitions contain the FHIR-20394 language plus later FHIR-37363 answer-validation guidance. Current core source only has OID entries and item-type wording that references the extension URLs, which is not misleading without duplicating the extension comments. FHIR-30581 is SDC IG background for an explicit off-list-unit mechanism and does not reverse the default required-list interpretation.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source hunk was made because the authoritative extension definitions are already correct outside the core checkout, and duplicating their constraint in remaining core item-type text would be redundant and drift-prone.
